Our new dryer stopped heating and after reading various posts online determined this was the likely cause. Easy swap out and confirmed the old one had blown. This fixed things right up and we are back in business. Saved a ton of time and frustration if we had to call out a technician.

I cannot fault the product itself, but would offer a hard-learned lesson.  You will see many reviews concerning repair of your heating problems, but FIRST check the voltage going to your dryer! I bought three separate parts trying to get my dryer to heat properly only to find out that my circuit breaker had become partially detached from the breaker box. I had about lost my mind trying to figure out why nothing I did remedied the heating issue, and I thought the repairman had when he asked if I knew the voltage going to the dryer. The drum needs 110v to spin, but the heating element requires 220v. (If you find this review useful, PLEASE tap the button below. Thanks!)

Items arrived in such a timely manner, I was shocked! I ordered on Saturday (2/6) and they arrived late Monday (2/8) afternoon! My dad stopped by after work last night (2/9) to switch the parts out, and after doing so, my dryer had heat again! It was as if Satan himself were blowing sweet heat into the dryer, and let me tell you, it brought me endless joy to know I wouldn't have to go to our shady town laundromat to pay to have my clothes dried.

I started out with one towel. Yes, I understand and appreciate the absurdity of only having one towel to wash, but it just so happened to be the case, and I wanted to start the dryer off small and ease it back into the work rotation after its illness. No issues whatsoever! My next load was work scrubs and thermal tees that I wear underneath said scrubs, as it's been pretty cold lately. I heard the dryer buzzer go off and was instantly suspicious, as I know the length of time it takes the machine to dry a load of laundry. I went downstairs to check on it, and sure enough, the washer was still in final spin cycle. The shade I threw at this dryer was so dark and cold, it would have made a forest proud. Upon checking, the scrubs were dry but cool. The thermal tees were damp. After turning the machine on again and letting it run for about 5 minutes, I opened the door to confirm that, again, the dryer was not heating up.
